terms.comment: The bronze cymbals of the rites of Cybele and Bacchus; the genitive plural is cymbalum in Catullus (63.21).
Classically a vinegar cup, any small cup, and the juggler’s cup (Sen. Ep. 45.7); the cymbal is a medieval sense. Morgan–Owens and Andresian spell it acitābulum.

phrases.latin: Mūsica īnstrūmenta sunt, quae ēdunt vōcem: prīmō, cum pulsantur, ut cymbalum pistillō, tintinnābulum intus globulō ferreō, crepitāculum circumversandō …
phrases.english: Musical instruments are things that make a sound: first, those that are struck, like the cymbal with a striker, the bell with a little iron ball inside, the rattle by being turned round …

sources: Lewis & Short: cymbalum · Lewis & Short: acetabulum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. percussion: cymbal.
Comenius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-comenius).
